# A Year in My Soundtrack

> How did my music obsessions change throughout the year?

> Let's load the data and read in the json files I received from Spotify website.

```{r}
library(jsonlite)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

files <- list.files(
  "data/Spotify_Account_Data",
  pattern = "StreamingHistory_music_.*\\.json$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

files

spotify <- map_dfr(files, fromJSON)

glimpse(spotify)
```

> Now we need to clean the data in a way we can understand and analyze better!

```{r}
spotify_clean <- spotify %>%
  select(
    endTime,
    artistName,
    trackName,
    msPlayed
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    datetime = as.POSIXct(endTime, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M", tz = "UTC"),
    date = as.Date(datetime),
    hour = as.integer(format(datetime, "%H")),
    day = format(datetime, "%A"),
    month = format(datetime, "%Y-%m"),
    minutesPlayed = msPlayed / 60000
  )

glimpse(spotify_clean)
```

```{r}
range(spotify_clean$date, na.rm = TRUE)
```

> We have almost exactly a year worth of listening data!

```{r}
sum(spotify_clean$minutesPlayed, na.rm = TRUE)
```

```{r}
spotify_clean %>%
  count(artistName, sort = TRUE) %>%
  head(20)
```

> And this is my 20 most frequent played artists!

```{r}
artist_minutes <- spotify_clean %>%
  filter(artistName != "Unknown Artist") %>%
  group_by(artistName) %>%
  summarise(
    minutes = sum(minutesPlayed, na.rm = TRUE),
    plays = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(minutes))

head(artist_minutes, 20)
```

> This gives us my actual top artists by listening time.

> Now let's calculate artist and the month

```{r}
monthly_artist <- spotify_clean %>%
  filter(artistName != "Unknown Artist") %>%
  group_by(month, artistName) %>%
  summarise(
    minutes = sum(minutesPlayed, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

top_artists <- artist_minutes %>%
  slice_head(n = 12) %>%
  pull(artistName)

monthly_top <- monthly_artist %>%
  filter(artistName %in% top_artists)

monthly_top
```

> Let's start visualizing

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

monthly_top <- monthly_artist %>%
  filter(artistName %in% top_artists) %>%
  complete(
    month,
    artistName,
    fill = list(minutes = 0)
  )

ggplot(
  monthly_top,
  aes(
    x = month,
    y = artistName,
    fill = minutes
  )
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "C",
    name = "Minutes listened"
  ) +
  labs(
  title = "A Year in My Soundtrack",
  subtitle = "Amy Winehouse is my top listened artist this year",
  x = NULL,
  y = NULL, 
  caption = "*My top 12 frequently listened artists and their change against months. \nData: Spotify User Data, Spotify, Week of October 5th, 2026.\nCreated by Riley Karatas | Creation date: October 5th, 2026."
) +
theme_minimal() +
theme(
  axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
  panel.grid = element_blank(),
  plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0),
  plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0),
  plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
)

```

> The conlcusion is that I listen to a lot of Amy Winehouse depending on the month.
> It seems that my taste in music is quite international with Russian, Turkish, French Afro-beat and English songs.

# My PVJ After First Round of Edits

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

monthly_top <- monthly_artist %>%
  filter(artistName %in% top_artists) %>%
  complete(
    month,
    artistName,
    fill = list(minutes = 0)
  )

# Reorder months to start from January
month_order <- monthly_top %>%
  distinct(month) %>%
  mutate(
    month_num = as.integer(format(as.Date(paste0(month, "-01")), "%m")),
    year_part = as.integer(format(as.Date(paste0(month, "-01")), "%Y"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(month_num, year_part) %>%
  pull(month)

month_labels <- setNames(
  format(as.Date(paste0(month_order, "-01")), "%b %Y"),
  month_order
)

monthly_top <- monthly_top %>%
  mutate(
    month = factor(month, levels = month_order),
    minutes_bin = cut(
      minutes,
      breaks = c(-1, 25, 75, 150, 250, Inf),
      labels = c("0–25", "25–75", "75–150", "150–250", "250+")
    )
  )

ggplot(
  monthly_top,
  aes(
    x = month,
    y = artistName,
    fill = minutes_bin
  )
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(
    option = "C",
    name = "Minutes listened"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = month_labels) +
  labs(
    title = "A Year in My Soundtrack",
    subtitle = "Amy Winehouse is my top listened artist this year",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    caption = "*My top 12 frequently listened artists and their change against months. \nData: Spotify User Data, Spotify, Week of October 5th, 2026.\nCreated by Riley Karatas | Creation date: October 5th, 2026."
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )
```

    library(ggplot2)

        x = month,

        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
      )

## PVJ 3RD ROUND OF EDITS

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)

monthly_top <- monthly_artist %>%
  filter(artistName %in% top_artists) %>%
  complete(
    month,
    artistName,
    fill = list(minutes = 0)
  )

# Order months chronologically by actual date, not by month-number-then-year
month_order <- monthly_top %>%
  distinct(month) %>%
  mutate(month_date = as.Date(paste0(month, "-01"))) %>%
  arrange(month_date) %>%
  pull(month)

# Two-line x-axis labels: month on top, year only where it changes
month_labels <- sapply(seq_along(month_order), function(i) {
  d   <- as.Date(paste0(month_order[i], "-01"))
  mon <- format(d, "%b")
  yr  <- format(d, "%Y")
  if (i == 1 || format(as.Date(paste0(month_order[i - 1], "-01")), "%Y") != yr) {
    paste0(mon, "\n", yr)
  } else {
    mon
  }
})
names(month_labels) <- month_order

monthly_top <- monthly_top %>%
  mutate(
    month = factor(month, levels = month_order),
    artistName = factor(artistName, levels = rev(top_artists)),
    minutes_bin = cut(
      minutes,
      breaks = c(-1, 25, 75, 150, 250, Inf),
      labels = c("0–25", "25–75", "75–150", "150–250", "250+")
    )
  )

ggplot(
  monthly_top,
  aes(
    x = month,
    y = artistName,
    fill = minutes_bin
  )
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(
    option = "C",
    name = "Minutes listened"
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = month_labels) +
  labs(
    # No str_wrap here anymore so it stays on one line
    title = "A month-by-month look at my most-played artists, led by Amy Winehouse",
    subtitle = str_wrap(
      "Amy Winehouse anchors nearly every month, but a few artists like Qendresa and GIMS surge briefly before fading out again.",
      width = 90
    ),
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    caption = "My top 12 frequently listened artists in descending order and their change against months. \nData: Spotify User Data, Spotify, Week of October 5th, 2026.\nCreated by Riley Karatas | Created on October 5th, 2026."
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    # Smaller + no wrap so the full line fits across the plot width
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0, face = "bold", size = 13),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 10.5, color = "grey40", lineheight = 1.1),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, color = "grey40"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),
    # Artist names now black instead of the default grey
    axis.text.y = element_text(color = "black"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.justification = "left",
    legend.title = element_text(hjust = 0),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 10, r = 15, b = 10, l = 10)
  )
```

## PVJ 4th ROUND OF EDITS

```{r}
# Shorter subtitle
subtitle_text <- "Amy Winehouse anchors nearly every month, with brief surges from Qendresa and GIMS."

for (a in highlight_artists) {
  subtitle_text <- str_replace(
    subtitle_text,
    fixed(a),
    paste0("**", a, "**")
  )
}

ggplot(
  monthly_top,
  aes(
    x = month,
    y = artistName,
    fill = minutes_bin
  )
) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = bin_colors,
    labels = bin_labels,
    name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = month_labels) +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = y_labels) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "A month-by-month look at my most-played artists",
    subtitle = str_wrap(subtitle_text, width = 90),
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "Created by Riley Karatas on October 5th, 2026, based on data from Spotify ",
      "User Data\n",
      "My top 12 frequently listened artists in descending order and their change against months."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_family = "Georgia") +
  theme(
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    
    plot.title = element_text(
      hjust = 0, face = "bold", size = 13
    ),
    
    plot.subtitle = element_markdown(
      hjust = 0, size = 9.5,
      color = "grey40", lineheight = 1.1
    ),
    
    plot.caption = element_text(
      hjust = 0,
      size = 7.5,
      color = "grey60",
      margin = margin(t = 14)
    ),
    
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, size = 8.5
    ),
    
    axis.text.y = element_markdown(
      color = "black", size = 8.5
    ),
    
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    
    # --- key changes for white space ---
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.justification = "center",   # was "left"
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8.5),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm"),
    legend.margin = margin(t = -5),
    
    plot.margin = margin(t = 10, r = 15, b = 16, l = 10)
  )
```
